Maria K: quick question — we keep hitting odd failures when mixing old safetensors headers with the new compact index. Is it worth doing an explicit serializer version field in the shard header now?
Sam T: yes, we should. current heuristic (magic + flags) is fragile when we start adding streaming-friendly markers.
Kai: agree. proposal: add `format_version` u8 and an optional `compat_mask` byte. loader checks version and mask to decide fast-path vs compatibility shim.
Anita P: curious about the shim cost — if a loader detects old version, do we fall back to full index-first warmup or can we stream with on-the-fly index synth?
Sam T: streaming+on-the-fly index synth is possible but complexity spikes. cheapest safe fallback is index-first warmup for that model version.
Maria K: we need a gradation: prefer streaming when header has live-offsets table present, otherwise index-first. so header bits should advertise `offset_table_present` and `checksum_algo`.
Kai: +1. also include a 32-bit stable checksum (not just CRC) to detect partial writes on hotpatch.
Luis: for onboarding older checkpoints, can we include a small sidecar manifest with mapping to new header tokens? That avoids rewriting blobs during rollout.
Anita P: sidecar helps but is operationally messy for Dedicated/private customers. I'd rather make header self-sufficient and have a tiny conversion utility for on-disk bundles.
Sam T: tradeoff: bigger header increases seek cost in tiny-object stores and slightly bigger first-byte latency. But it's only a couple dozen bytes — worth for correctness.
Kai: runtime compatibility decisions: loader API should expose `Loader::capabilities()` so orchestrator can route requests to nodes that support desired features (streaming offsets, atomic hotpatch).
Maria K: +1. That keeps routing decoupled from loader internals. Add a `requires_index_first` bit in capability set.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: eng-ml/model-loader-v2 (canary) -> infra-canary-3 at 2026-05-02T03:00Z
Luis: for canary, let's enable `format_version=2` but keep a fallback heuristic that logs and doesn't fail requests. We need heavy metrics: %fallback, avg extra latency, bytes read.
Anita P: logging note: avoid logging raw header bytes in prod. emit structured metric tags: version, offset_table_present, checksum_ok.
Sam T: on hotpatching: define atomic swap semantics: write new shard to temp path, fsync, then rename. header must include monotonic `bundle_epoch` so older processes reject new-if-not-compatible.
Kai: also consider a lightweight compatibility manifest baked into the control-plane: model-id -> supported_format_versions. This allows the router to serve older clients with older nodes.
Maria K: long-term: aim for index-first optionality per-model. Some models (short context) get better streaming perf; others (huge) prefer index-first. Keep per-model policy in model catalog.
Luis: action items: (1) spec header v2 fields (format_version, compat_mask, offset_table_present, checksum_algo, bundle_epoch) — Kai + Sam, (2) loader API `capabilities()` — Maria, (3) conversion tool for on-disk bundles to v2 — Luis, (4) canary metrics dashboard — Anita.
Anita P: i'll stub grafana panels and add alerts for >1% fallback rate or checksum failures.
Maria K: thanks team. i'll write a short follow-up RFC with the header bytes layout and examples of the rename/fsync hotpatch pattern.
Sam T: small nit — use SHA256 truncated 16 bytes for checksum to avoid collisions on hotpatch.
Kai: ok. if we adopt truncated SHA256, note we have to document algorithm id and truncate length in header.
Maria K: noted. i'll include migration guidance (how to convert sidecar manifests, how to run conversion tool on Dedicated).
Luis: i'll start the conversion script draft and drop a PoC in the repo.
Maria K: cool. closing this thread — feel free to ping me for RFC review. :thumbsup:
